title: Iterative minimization in reduced density matrix functional theory for periodic systems
authors: Kai Luo, Jingang Han, Peize Lin, Daye Zheng, Mohan Chen, Xinguo Ren
abstract: Reduced density matrix functional theory (RDMFT) offers a route beyond Kohn-Sham density functional theory for strongly correlated systems, yet practical calculations for periodic solids are still out of reach. We formulate RDMFT for extended systems in a basis-independent way and present a planewave implementation using iterative minimization for periodic solids, evaluating nonlocal exchange-correlation functionals through the existing adaptive compressed exchange machinery. Natural occupations are optimized under N-representability constraints with a spectral projected gradient (SPG) method or an first-order explicit-by-implicit (EBI) map, while natural orbitals are updated by Riemannian optimization on the complex Stiefel manifolds. Benchmarks on typical systems of \ce{H2}, silicon, and sodium with the Hartree-Fock functional show that SPG reproduces converged hybrid references, whereas EBI can stall when occupations approach $0$ or $1$. With the power and Müller functionals, SPG yields lower energies and more stable convergence than EBI. Applications to fractionally charged \ce{LiH}, dissociating \ce{H2} and \ce{N2} molecules, and equation of state of silicon show that the algorithm presented in this implementation is reliable and robust.
summary: This paper presents a robust and basis-independent implementation of Reduced Density Matrix Functional Theory (RDMFT) tailored for periodic solids. It tackles the computational challenge by using iterative minimization techniques, such as Spectral Projected Gradient (SPG), to optimize natural occupations within k-space. The method is validated on several materials, demonstrating its reliability for calculating ground state properties like energy and equation of state.
main_problem: Developing a robust and efficient Reduced Density Matrix Functional Theory (RDMFT) formulation for calculating ground-state properties of periodic, strongly correlated solids.
main_result: The proposed implementation using the Spectral Projected Gradient (SPG) method is shown to be numerically stable and reliable across various benchmarks, yielding better convergence than alternative methods like EBI.
method: The authors formulate RDMFT for extended systems in a basis-independent way, employing iterative minimization techniques (SPG/EBI) to optimize natural occupations under N-representability constraints within a k-resolved framework.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to periodic solids like H2, silicon, and sodium, extending the formalism from molecular systems. The energy functional is minimized with respect to the one-body reduced density matrix (1-RDM), which is decomposed into k-resolved parts.
key_observables: Ground state energy, electron momentum density, equation of state (EOS) for silicon, and spectral functions.
important_parameters: Electron number ($N$), occupation numbers ($n_i$) constrained between 0 and 1, and the Brillouin-zone weights ($w_{\mathbf{k}}$).
main_assumptions: The calculation relies on approximating the unknown exchange-correlation energy functional ($E_{xc}[\gamma]$) using separable kernels (e.g., Power or Müller functionals).
figures_summary: Figure 6 compares Silicon EOS results obtained using various approximations, including PBE, HF, PBE0, and specialized power/Müller functionals.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general RDMFT formulation for periodic systems to detailing the k-resolved 1-RDM structure. It then focuses on the iterative minimization procedure, comparing optimization algorithms (SPG vs EBI) before presenting benchmark results on various materials and properties like EOS.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the rigorous development of constrained optimization techniques (like SPG) for high-dimensional quantum many-body Hamiltonians is highly relevant to developing scalable methods for strongly correlated systems in AMO physics.
